label: Mid-original-phase steps (t=4-6) in sequences starting with 3 that contain z/g, peaking on q after g
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.04% of steps). It fires almost only in the original phase (97.5% of mass), at steps 4-6 (t=4 and t=5 together hold ~89% of mass), and never in the copy phase; a small amount fires at the delimiter when the output is 3. The strongest conditioning is first_tok == 3 (20x lift, 72% of mass). Inputs seen earlier also matter: z and g in the prefix (prev2_tok z 10x, prev_tok g 12x). The current input matters too: q gives 9.6x lift. The largest activations are on q right after g in sequences starting with 3 (e.g. 3 e z g [q]). The predicate first_tok=3 & seen(z or g) & t in 4..6 reaches dev F1 ~0.23 and mass recall ~0.53, and precision is low (~0.15): most steps matching this context do not fire. The feature looks like a conjunctive hidden-state direction that no simple predicate captures. It does not fire at t<3, in the copy phase, or at t>=8.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=3 (+7.47), prev_tok=g (+5.28), orig1=e (+3.94), orig0=h (+3.54), t=5 (+3.34), orig2=z (+3.31). Lower it: orig2=d (-3.14), prev3_tok=- (-3.02), orig_idx=-1 (-2.71), orig1=i (-2.63).
